records.title: Kubota BX2380 Tractor Specs, PTO Power, Weight & Hydraulic Data
records.excerpt: Kubota BX2380 source-checked specifications: 21.6 gross engine HP, 17.7 PTO HP, 540-rpm rear PTO, 6.6 US-gallon fuel tank, and published 1,455-lb base weight.
records.content:
The Kubota BX2380 is a four-wheel-drive sub-compact tractor intended for property upkeep, mowing and light implement work. For owners comparing machines, the important figures are not just the gross engine horsepower: PTO power, hitch lifting capacity, transmission type and the weight of the actual configuration all affect what the tractor can do.

BX2380 key specifications at a glance

Kubota's US detailed-specification sheet reports 21.6 gross engine HP and 17.7 PTO HP, both at an engine speed of 3,200 rpm. It identifies the engine as the three-cylinder, liquid-cooled Kubota D902 diesel. The tractor uses a hydrostatic transmission with two speed ranges and is four-wheel-drive.

Rear PTO, mid PTO and three-point hitch

The published rear PTO speed is 540 rpm, while the mid PTO runs at 2,500 rpm. These numbers describe PTO shaft speeds, not the engine RPM required for every implement. The three-point hitch is SAE Category 1. Kubota publishes a 680-lb lift capacity at 24 inches behind the lift points, compared with 1,213 lb at the lift points. When comparing a hitch or implement, use the same measurement point rather than the larger number alone.

Hydraulics and weight

The US detailed sheet distinguishes 5.2 US gpm of hydraulic pump output from 1.0 US gpm of power-steering pump output, for 6.2 US gpm total hydraulic flow. This matters because total pump flow must not be confused with flow available to a particular auxiliary circuit. The sheet lists a 1,455-lb base weight; installed implements, ballast, tires and optional equipment can change a working machine's actual mass.

Fuel and service planning

The published fuel tank capacity is 6.6 US gallons. Kubota's detailed sheet also contains separate capacities for the engine crankcase, coolant and transmission case; do not substitute those volumes for the amount required in every drain-and-refill procedure without consulting the correct operator manual.

Who should compare the BX2380?

It is worth considering alongside the John Deere 1025R for work on lawns, driveways, light landscaping and small properties. Buyers with heavier three-point implements should also examine larger compact models such as the Kubota L2502 HST. Overall tractor size, hitch specifications, ballast and the implement maker's requirements matter more than engine horsepower by itself.

Source and configuration notes

These figures come from Kubota USA's BX2380 Detailed Specifications (PDF). Some Kubota regional pages and product revisions report different weights or options. Confirm the specific tractor's model identification and operator manual before maintenance or load handling.

specs.fms_configuration_notes: US BX2380 detailed sheet; 4WD HST; total hydraulic flow includes steering; 1,455 lb published base weight, not loaded operating weight; 680 lb hitch lift rated 24 in behind lift points.

records.title: John Deere 1025R Specs, 24 HP Engine, PTO & Weight
records.excerpt: Manufacturer-backed John Deere 1025R tractor specs, including 24 rated engine horsepower, 18 PTO horsepower, 6.3 gpm rated pump output, limited Category 1 hitch and 1,556-lb base weight.
records.content:
The John Deere 1025R is a sub-compact utility tractor for mowing, loader use, snow clearing and property chores. John Deere lists a hydrostatic two-range transmission, four-wheel drive and a limited Category 1 rear hitch. To assess equipment compatibility, compare rated PTO power and attachment requirements, not just the engine's headline horsepower.

Engine and PTO power are different

John Deere's current US product information identifies the 1025R with a Yanmar 3TNV80F-NCJT engine and 24 hp rated engine power (SAE J1995). Its published rated PTO power is 18 hp. The difference is relevant when selecting a mower, snowblower, chipper or other PTO-driven implement: an implement's minimum PTO power requirement is not interchangeable with the tractor's gross engine-power figure.

Hydraulics, transmission and hitch

John Deere specifies a two-range hydrostatic transmission and limited Category 1 hitch. The manufacturer lists a 6.3 US-gpm rated hydraulic pump output. A combined flow figure does not by itself establish what an external hydraulic attachment will receive; check the exact circuit and implement's pressure and flow requirements.

Weight and attachment decisions

The US specification lists 1,556 lb as base machine weight. This is not a measured in-use weight with a loader, loaded tires, ballast, mower or backhoe. When evaluating lifting or towing, refer to the rated attachment specifications and the operator manual for the exact configuration.

What to check before buying

  • Confirm whether the tractor has the loader, mower and attachment couplers required for your work.
  • Verify rear hitch category, PTO arrangement and PTO power against each implement's requirements.
  • Check storage height, transport weight and ground conditions for your property.
  • Inspect the actual tractor and ask for service records if buying used.

How does it compare?

For a compact machine designed for similar property-maintenance tasks, review the Kubota BX2380. For higher weight and a larger tractor class, look at the Kubota L2502 HST. The comparison tool shows recorded figures side by side, with source and configuration cautions.

Original reference

Figures above are taken from John Deere's official US 1025R product specification, checked on the date below. Product descriptions and specifications may change. Always use the correct official manual for the specific serial number.

specs.fms_configuration_notes: US John Deere 1025R listing; rated engine power (SAE J1995); 6.3 US gpm rated pump output; weight is base machine weight, without optional attachments/ballast. Confirm model year and installed configuration.

records.title: Kubota L2502 HST 4WD Specs: Horsepower, PTO, Hitch & Weight
records.excerpt: US Kubota L2502 HST 4WD specs from the manufacturer: 24.8 gross HP, 19 PTO HP, Category 1 three-point hitch, 1,389-lb hitch lift 24 inches behind, and 2,833-lb ROPS weight.
records.content:
The Kubota L2502 HST 4WD belongs to Kubota's Standard L compact tractor family. This page focuses on the hydrostatic, four-wheel-drive configuration; the gear-drive version has a different PTO-power figure and other configuration differences. That distinction is essential when comparing tractors for mowing, field maintenance or loader work.

Engine and PTO horsepower

In the US L02 specification sheet, Kubota states 24.8 gross engine HP for the L2502 and 19.0 PTO HP for the HST version. The gear-drive L2502 has a different published PTO rating, so a specification marked simply “L2502 PTO horsepower” is not always precise enough for equipment selection. The L2502 uses a three-cylinder, direct-injection diesel.

Hitch and hydraulic capabilities

The L2502 uses an SAE Category I three-point hitch. Kubota rates its rear hitch at 1,874 lb at the lift points and 1,389 lb at 24 inches behind those points. This is a hitch rating, not the loader's bucket or pallet-fork rating. The brochure reports 5.2 US gpm for the main hydraulic pump and a separate 3.1 US gpm for power steering. Do not assume either number represents usable flow through a particular remote hydraulic connection.

Transmission and rear PTO

The HST 4WD is equipped with a three-range hydrostatic transmission. Kubota describes its HST rear PTO as a live-independent hydraulic PTO with wet brake. The US sheet specifies 540 rpm rear PTO speed at approximately 2,020 engine rpm for this variant.

Weight, fuel capacity and ballast

The manufacturer's US specification sheet lists a 2,833-lb weight with ROPS for the HST 4WD configuration and an 11.1-US-gallon fuel tank. ROPS weight is not a guarantee of the mass of a field-ready tractor; loaders, wheel weights, fluid-filled tires and mounted implements will change it. Match ballast and tire pressure to the operator manual and the intended task.

Comparing tractor size classes

The L2502 HST is a larger and heavier compact tractor than a sub-compact machine such as the Kubota BX2380. Consider storage, turning space, implement weight, PTO requirement and ground conditions before assuming the larger tractor is always better. Use our side-by-side comparison to see the published numbers and inspect their measurement notes.

Source and regional differences

Data on this page comes from Kubota USA L02 specifications (PDF). Canadian and other regional Kubota pages may list different engine or PTO values for similarly named variants. This record specifically uses the US HST 4WD brochure, not values mixed from other versions.

specs.fms_configuration_notes: US L2502 HST 4WD; 19.0 PTO HP (gear-drive has different rating); 2,833 lb with ROPS, without field options; hitch 1,389 lb 24 in behind lift points; main hydraulic pump 5.2 gpm separate from steering 3.1 gpm.

records.title: Tractor Engine HP vs PTO HP: What Each Rating Really Means
records.excerpt: Engine horsepower and PTO horsepower are not the same. Learn why implement sizing depends on the tractor's PTO rating, operating conditions and manufacturer requirements.
records.content:
When choosing a tractor, it is easy to compare the largest horsepower number on the brochure. But the number that helps you select a rotary cutter, chipper or other shaft-driven implement is often PTO horsepower, not headline engine horsepower. Both numbers matter, yet they describe different parts of the machine.

What is engine horsepower?

Engine horsepower describes the engine's mechanical power under the manufacturer's specified rating conditions. A published figure may be described as gross, net or rated power, and testing methods differ. Never assume an engine number measured under one standard is directly identical to a competing manufacturer's differently labeled figure.

What is PTO horsepower?

Power take-off horsepower is power available at the tractor's PTO shaft under specified test and rating conditions. Power losses through the drivetrain and PTO mechanism mean it is usually lower than engine horsepower. For a PTO-powered mower, baler, blower or chipper, the implement manufacturer's minimum required PTO horsepower is the more relevant starting point.

Three actual manufacturer examples

Tractor and configurationPublished engine HPPublished PTO HP
John Deere 1025R24 rated HP18 HP
Kubota BX238021.6 gross HP17.7 HP
Kubota L2502 HST 4WD24.8 gross HP19.0 HP

These are published numbers for specific models and configurations, not independent test results. The engine ratings use manufacturer's labeling, which is why the table keeps the word “rated” or “gross” next to each figure.

How to size an implement using PTO HP

  1. Find the implement's official minimum and maximum PTO-power requirements. These should be stated in its manual or manufacturer specifications.
  2. Locate your tractor's matching PTO rating. Confirm year, transmission, engine and applicable conditions; two variants of the same model can have different PTO horsepower.
  3. Confirm shaft speed and connection. Many rear implements are designed for a 540-rpm PTO; others need a different speed, spline or drive arrangement.
  4. Check physical and hydraulic requirements too. Hitch category, lift capability at the specified point, implement weight, ballast and any hydraulic pressure or flow requirements can be the limiting factor even when power is sufficient.
  5. Review safety requirements. PTO guarding, shear protection, operator position and the machine's original manual take priority over general sizing rules.

Does more engine HP always mean more usable implement power?

No. Transmission and PTO systems vary. For example, Kubota's L2502 US specification gives different PTO-power ratings for the gear-drive and HST versions even though they share the L2502 model designation. That is why a single number from a forum or dealer ad can be misleading unless the configuration is identified.

What about loader jobs and towing?

PTO horsepower is not a loader rating. Loader capacity is constrained by rated hydraulic performance, lift geometry, tractor/ballast stability and attachment weight. For towing or pulling implements, traction, tractor weight, gearing and drawbar limits may matter more than a PTO power figure.

Sources

Compare the official John Deere 1025R, Kubota BX2380 detailed specification and Kubota L02 specification sheet. Specific equipment questions should be resolved with the current manuals for both tractor and implement. Sources checked 2026-11-23.

records.title: Kubota BX2380 Fluid Capacities: Engine Oil, Coolant, Transmission & Fuel
records.excerpt: Kubota BX2380 manufacturer-listed fluid capacities: engine crankcase 3.5 US qt with filter, coolant 3.3 US qt, transmission case 3.0 US gal and fuel tank 6.6 US gal. Verify your manual.
records.content:
Looking up the Kubota BX2380 engine oil capacity is straightforward once the correct source and unit are clear. Kubota's US detailed specification lists a crankcase capacity of 3.5 US quarts with the filter. However, a catalog capacity is not a substitute for the correct refill-and-level procedure: the final level must always be confirmed using the manufacturer's instructions and the tractor's dipstick or specified level check.

Kubota BX2380 manufacturer-published capacities

SystemPublished capacity (US units)Approximate metric equivalent
Engine crankcase, with filter3.5 US qt3.31 L
Engine coolant3.3 US qt3.12 L
Coolant recovery tank0.4 US qt0.38 L
Transmission case3.0 US gal11.36 L
Fuel tank6.6 US gal24.98 L

Metric values are conversions of the published US figures, rounded to two decimal places. They are not separately quoted manufacturer capacities. This sheet describes the BX2380; do not apply its numbers automatically to BX1880, BX2680, BX23S or another tractor model.

Capacity is not the same as the refill quantity

A listed system capacity may differ from the amount you need during a routine service. Fluid can remain in passages, coolers and components after draining, and drain procedures vary. Use the exact operator manual and replace the correct filter where the procedure requires one. Add fluid according to the proper service instructions and verify the level before operating.

Which engine oil and hydraulic fluid should I use?

The specification table quoted here establishes volumes, not a universal recommendation for viscosity or replacement fluid. Engine oil viscosity, diesel classification, transmission/hydraulic fluid and coolant chemistry must be selected from the operator manual that applies to your market, serial number and ambient temperature. Do not mix fluids based only on a retailer's general compatibility list.

Safe inspection checklist

  • Park on suitable level ground, lower attached implements and make the tractor secure according to its manual.
  • Allow the engine and fluid systems to cool before servicing; pressurized hot coolant can cause severe burns.
  • Identify the engine, transmission and other reservoirs correctly before opening any filler or drain point.
  • Use clean containers and protect open ports from dirt; hydraulic contamination can damage components.
  • Verify the fluid level as the manufacturer specifies after servicing, and check for leaks before returning to work.

Where the numbers come from

The values above are from Kubota USA BX2380 Detailed Specifications, page 2, checked 2026-11-23. Always give the official operator manual priority over a general reference page for the correct fluid specification, level-check method and service interval.

See the full Kubota BX2380 specifications or convert US and metric units.

records.title: Kubota BX90 vs BX80: 2027 Models, HP, Loaders & What Changed
records.excerpt: Kubota's new BX90 series arrives in early 2027. Compare BX2190, BX2390 and BX2690 with the older BX80 platform, including engine HP, loader choices, controls and unknowns.
records.content:
Kubota's next generation of US sub-compact tractors is the BX90 Series. Announced on September 29, 2026, this redesign introduces five named models, new loader and mower options, and different operator controls. Kubota says the new series is scheduled to reach authorized US dealerships in early 2027. That means buyers evaluating a BX80 tractor in late 2026 should distinguish an already listed BX80 model from a BX90 model that may not yet be on a dealer lot.

Which models are in the new BX90 series?

The manufacturer identifies three main trim levels plus two tractor-loader-backhoe variants. These are actual announced US model names, not an estimated naming pattern:

BX90 modelPublished gross engine HPManufacturer-described focus
BX219019.3Entry-level BX90 with LA355 loader option
BX2390 Deluxe21.6Upgraded controls and compatibility with LA405 loader
BX2690 Premium23.9Advanced display and programmable engine settings
BX2390SNot separately stated in this announcementBackhoe-equipped configuration with BT604
BX2690S PremiumNot separately stated in this announcementPremium backhoe-equipped configuration with BT604 and LA405

The engine power figures above are gross engine horsepower stated for the three core trims. They are not PTO horsepower, and the announcement does not provide a complete model-by-model PTO and hydraulic specification table.

What changes from the BX80 platform?

1. Loader configurations and published lift ratings

The BX90 announcement names the redesigned LA355 and LA405 loaders, with respective advertised lift capacities of up to 721 lb and 904 lb. It also mentions twin bucket cylinders, protected hose routing and easier mounting alignment. Those numbers are loader-specific announced ratings, not a guarantee of the lifting capacity of every BX90 configuration at every load position.

The existing BX80 US product page quotes a 739-lb series maximum loader-lift capacity. Do not subtract one number from the other and call it an apples-to-apples performance increase: comparisons require the exact loader, measurement point (such as pivot pin or 500 mm forward), height and configuration from the relevant official specifications.

2. Mower decks and attachment convenience

Kubota describes new 54-inch and 60-inch welded-steel mower decks with pin-on or drive-over configurations. It also introduces an available Swift-Mount auto-coupling driveline, intended to simplify deck attachment. Existing BX80 tractors already have mower deck choices, so the practical buying question is whether the exact deck and attachment process fit your routine, storage and mowing conditions.

3. Operator controls

One noticeable redesign is the BX90's side-by-side forward and reverse HST pedals. The BX80 platform uses Kubota's treadle-style foot control. Buyers accustomed to one layout should try the new one at a dealer rather than assume a specification sheet can answer ergonomic preferences.

4. Trim-level differences

The BX2390 Deluxe adds electronically controlled PTO engagement, position control for the three-point hitch and telescopic stabilizers. The BX2690 Premium adds a color LCD display, programmable engine-speed settings and a joystick-integrated throttle-up function. These features should not be assumed present on the entry BX2190.

5. New backhoe-equipped models

Kubota also announced BX2390S and BX2690S Premium tractor-loader-backhoe packages with the BT604 backhoe, a flip-up seat and an automatic stabilizer lock. Loader/backhoe package mass and compatibility with other implements will need the individual product and operator documentation when it becomes available.

BX2380 versus BX2390: what can we actually compare?

ItemBX2380 (BX80)BX2390 Deluxe (BX90)
Gross engine HP21.621.6 announced
PTO horsepower17.7 from Kubota's detailed BX2380 sheetNot given in the BX90 launch announcement
HST direction controlTreadle-type pedalSide-by-side pedals
Loader platformBX80 loader options; confirm exact modelRedesigned LA405 compatibility
Retail availabilityExisting BX80 product familyKubota stated early 2027 availability

The unchanged 21.6 gross engine horsepower figure does not establish that every PTO, hydraulic or performance measurement is identical. See our Kubota BX2380 reference and guide to engine HP versus PTO HP for an explanation of how to compare the power ratings.

Which should a property owner consider?

For someone buying in late 2026 who needs a tractor immediately, a BX80 machine with the correct attachments and a verified service history may be an option worth evaluating. For a buyer able to wait for the announced 2027 BX90 arrival, the new controls, loader systems and mower coupling options justify a direct dealership demonstration. Neither choice should be made on gross horsepower alone.

Before committing, compare the actual quoted machine configuration, rated hydraulic and PTO specifications, attachments, transport and storage needs, and the total local dealer price. Kubota's announcement does not supply a final nationwide price list or every variant's full specifications, so those details must be checked separately.

Official manufacturer sources

Read the September 29, 2026 Kubota USA BX90 announcement and the Kubota USA BX80 Series overview. The BX2380's individual specification sheet is available from our BX2380 model page. These announcements describe product plans and technical features; specifications and equipment availability are subject to change.

records.title: KIOTI CK2620 Specs: 24.5 HP Gear-Drive Tractor, PTO & Hitch
records.excerpt: Source-checked KIOTI CK2620 gear-drive specs: 24.5 engine HP, 19.5 PTO HP, 12F/12R manual transmission, 9-gal fuel tank and published 2,634-lb weight.

specs.fms_configuration_notes: US CK2620 manual (12 forward/12 reverse gears). Manufacturer lists 11.7 gpm pump capacity, not confirmed auxiliary implement flow; 1,631 lb hitch lift rating without a 24-in measurement point. 2,634 lb published tractor weight; tires, loader, ballast and attachments affect working mass.

records.content:
The KIOTI CK2620 is a compact tractor built around a 24.5-horsepower diesel engine and a manual, gear-drive transmission. It is easy to confuse the CK2620 with the CK2620H, but the transmission and available PTO power are not identical. This reference focuses on the gear-drive CK2620 listed by KIOTI for the US market.

Engine: 24.5 horsepower

KIOTI identifies the engine as the 3A165LWM-U4 diesel and lists 24.50 engine horsepower with a displacement of 100.50 cubic inches (1,647 cc). The nine-US-gallon fuel tank is a published capacity, not a fuel-consumption estimate. Actual fuel use depends on engine load, ground conditions, attachment and operating technique.

Gear transmission and PTO: why it matters

The CK2620's manual transmission provides 12 forward and 12 reverse speeds in the manufacturer specifications. KIOTI publishes 19.50 PTO horsepower and a 540-rpm rear PTO. An optional 2,000-rpm mid PTO is also noted. Before ordering a mower, rotary cutter, post-hole digger or chipper, verify that the implement supports the exact available PTO power, shaft speed and shaft connection.

The hydrostatic CK2620H has a different PTO rating. Do not interpret the engine's 24.5 hp as the power available at the PTO shaft. Engine HP vs PTO HP explained describes the difference.

Hitch and hydraulic capacity

KIOTI lists a Category 1 three-point hitch with position control and a published 1,631-lb lift capacity for this manual configuration. The manufacturer page does not specify that the number is measured 24 inches behind the lift points. It is therefore not directly interchangeable with a rival's 24-inch-behind-hitch capacity.

The official table gives a hydraulic pump capacity of 11.70 US gallons per minute. That is not a promise that every remote valve or hydraulic implement receives 11.70 gpm. Ask the dealer for circuit-specific flow, coupler and pressure specifications for your exact equipment.

Dimensions and published weight

Manufacturer figureCK2620
Wheelbase65.7 in
Ground clearance13.4 in
Published tractor weight2,634 lb
Overall width54.5 in
Length with hitch120.9 in

Always check trailer and vehicle capacity against the actual loaded machine. A tractor carrying a front loader, ballast and rear attachment can weigh substantially more than an unconfigured published figure.

Is the manual CK2620 right for your work?

The practical attraction of the manual version is its mechanical gear selection and the published PTO horsepower available for driven implements. It may appeal to owners who prefer gear ratios for repeated pulling or PTO work. The HST variant may be more convenient for work with frequent directional changes, especially loader use, but neither transmission automatically guarantees greater pulling or lifting capacity.

Use Compare Equipment to examine this model alongside the CK2620H or similar compact tractors. Check tire type, ballast, loading geometry, the precise attachment and safety instructions before buying.

Primary reference

KIOTI US CK2620 manufacturer specifications, checked 2026-11-23. KIOTI notes that specifications may vary with axle, tire and attachment configuration and may change. Use the correct model's official manuals for repairs and safety-critical service.

records.title: KIOTI CK2620H Specs: HST Tractor Power, PTO & Weight
records.excerpt: KIOTI CK2620H hydrostatic compact tractor data: 24.5 engine HP, 18.7 PTO HP, 3-range HST, 540-rpm rear PTO, 9-gal fuel tank and published 2,689-lb weight.

specs.fms_configuration_notes: US CK2620H hydrostatic model with 3 speed ranges. 11.7 gpm published pump capacity, not validated flow at implement remotes. Website lists separate hydraulic/hitch lift entries; measurement point not established. 2,689 lb is the published tractor weight without assuming loader or ballast.

records.content:
The KIOTI CK2620H is the hydrostatic counterpart of the gear-drive CK2620. Both models are listed with 24.5 engine horsepower, but KIOTI publishes 18.7 PTO horsepower for the HST model, compared with 19.5 PTO hp for the manual version. It is a small but real distinction for buyers sizing PTO-driven implements.

Engine, fuel and drivetrain

The CK2620H is listed with KIOTI's 3A165LWM-U4 diesel engine, 100.50 cubic inches of displacement and 24.50 engine horsepower. The 9-US-gallon fuel capacity is common to the listed CK2620 models, but fuel efficiency and operating duration should not be inferred from that capacity alone.

Unlike the CK2620 manual's 12 forward and 12 reverse ratios, the CK2620H uses a three-range hydrostatic transmission. An HST transmission allows speed and direction modulation through the travel pedals, which may be useful during loader cycles and landscaping around buildings or obstacles. Ergonomics and operating preferences are individual; test the actual machine before deciding.

Rear PTO and hitch

The manufacturer specifies 18.70 PTO horsepower with a 540-rpm rear PTO and notes an optional 2,000-rpm mid PTO. For a rotary mower, tiller or chipper, check the implement's required PTO horsepower, rated shaft speed, recommended tractor size and guarding requirements. The engine's 24.5 hp is not a replacement for PTO rating.

KIOTI lists a Category 1 three-point hitch and position control. Its published specifications show hydraulic and hitch lift entries that are not identically labeled. Because the site does not clarify the hitch test point as 24 inches behind the lift points, we do not place an unsupported rating in the standardized 24-inch field in our comparison database.

Pump capacity and tractor weight

KIOTI reports 11.70 US gpm pump capacity. A pump figure is not the same as the output through a specified auxiliary connection or the loader's lifting force. For hydraulic attachments, confirm the circuit's actual flow, pressure and connector type with the dealer or factory documentation.

SpecificationCK2620H
Wheelbase65.7 inches
Minimum ground clearance13.4 inches
Published tractor weight2,689 lb
Rear PTO speed540 rpm
Fuel capacity9 US gallons

Actual transport weight depends on tires, loader, backhoe, ballast and fluid fill. Do not calculate a trailer rating solely from the published bare tractor mass.

CK2620 versus CK2620H

If your work means repeated forward/reverse movement and loader handling, HST controls may be a deciding factor. If you prefer a manual gearbox, compare the gear-drive CK2620 and its 19.5 PTO hp rating. Both configurations need the same careful evaluation of implement fitment, ground conditions, hydraulic connections and available dealer service.

Visit our comparison tool for their recorded specifications. Remember that shared engine output does not guarantee identical PTO output, dimensions, weight or service requirements.

Source

Manufacturer: KIOTI CK2620H US technical specifications, checked 2026-11-23. Specifications are subject to revision and may differ by axle, tire and attachment options; use the correct operator manual for service.

records.title: Kubota L3302 HST 4WD Specs: 33 HP, PTO, Hitch & Weight
records.excerpt: Kubota US L3302 HST specs: 33.0 gross engine HP, 26.1 PTO HP, 6.8 gpm main hydraulic pump, Category I hitch and 2,921-lb ROPS weight.

specs.fms_configuration_notes: Official US L02 brochure, L3302 HST 4WD column. Gross engine 33.0 hp (SAE J1995); PTO 26.1 hp; main hydraulic pump 6.8 US gpm plus separate power-steering pump 4.1 gpm. Three-point hitch 1,433 lb rated 24 in behind lift points. Weight 2,921 lb with ROPS; not loader-equipped operating weight.

records.content:
The Kubota L3302 HST 4WD is a Standard L compact tractor with a three-range hydrostatic transmission and a published 33.0 gross engine horsepower. This page uses the specific HST 4WD column from Kubota's US L02 specification brochure. The gear-drive L3302 shares the gross engine power figure but has a different PTO rating and weight.

Engine and PTO power

Kubota's brochure specifies a water-cooled three-cylinder diesel with a 1,826-cc displacement. Gross engine power is 33.0 HP under SAE J1995, while the net engine rating is 31.8 HP. Neither figure should be substituted for the machine's 26.1 PTO horsepower when sizing a driven implement.

The rear PTO is rated 540 rpm, with a corresponding engine speed of about 2,470 rpm listed for the HST variant. The PTO connection type, guarding and implement's recommended tractor horsepower must also match. The gear version lists 28.0 PTO hp, which is why mixed-specification comparison pages can give misleading results.

Three-point hitch ratings: measurement points matter

The manufacturer publishes 1,985 lb at the lift points and 1,433 lb measured 24 inches behind them for the L3302/L3902 series. For a mounted implement whose center of mass is rearward of the lift points, the 24-inch rating may be more useful as a reference, but it still does not determine safe handling for every attachment or operating condition. Confirm implement geometry, ballast and the official limits.

Hydraulic pump figures

Kubota lists 6.8 US gpm for the main hydraulic pump and a separate 4.1 US gpm for the power-steering pump. Do not use their combined total as if it were the flow supplied at a single remote valve. Hydraulic implements require an appropriate matching connection and pressure rating as well as flow.

Weight, wheelbase and fuel

Official US figureL3302 HST 4WD
Weight with ROPS2,921 lb
Wheelbase63.4 in
Minimum ground clearance13.4 in
Fuel capacity11.1 US gal
Rear PTO speed540 rpm

The weight above is the manufacturer-listed ROPS machine, not a tractor with a loader, filled tires, rear ballast and full complement of implements. Always calculate transport weight from the actual configuration.

When to choose the L3302 HST

The L3302 HST is worth evaluating for mixed property work where frequent speed adjustments and directional changes matter. Buyers requiring more PTO power can compare the L3902 HST, which has higher engine and PTO ratings in the same brochure. The official specification table lists the same hitch category, 24-inch hitch rating, hydraulic main-pump capacity and ROPS weight for those two HST variants, but that does not mean their performance is identical under load.

Also consider Kubota L2502 HST if tractor size and weight constraints are more important than maximum PTO horsepower. See the model comparison tool.

Primary source

Kubota Tractor Corporation: L02 Series US specification brochure, pages 14–15, checked 2026-11-23. Always use the correct operator manual and serial-specific information for service and safety.

records.title: Kubota L3902 HST 4WD Specs: 37.5 HP, PTO, Weight & Hitch
records.excerpt: Official US Kubota L3902 HST specs: 37.5 gross engine HP, 30.3 PTO HP, 6.8-gpm main pump, Category I hitch, 1,433-lb hitch capacity at 24 inches and 2,921-lb ROPS weight.

specs.fms_configuration_notes: US L02 specification brochure L3902 HST 4WD column: 37.5 gross HP SAE J1995; 30.3 PTO HP. 6.8 gpm main hydraulic pump and 4.1 gpm steering pump separately. Three-point lift 1,433 lb at 24 in behind lift points; 2,921 lb published ROPS weight without loader/ballast.

records.content:
The Kubota L3902 HST 4WD is a higher-powered Standard L compact tractor with a three-range hydrostatic transmission. Kubota's US L02 specification sheet lists 37.5 gross engine horsepower and 30.3 PTO horsepower for this particular configuration. Do not confuse this HST value with the 32.1 PTO hp rating listed for the gear-drive L3902.

Engine ratings and PTO horsepower

The L3902's manufacturer-listed diesel is a water-cooled three-cylinder unit with 1,826 cc displacement. Gross engine output is 37.5 hp, and net power is 36.3 hp, measured under the respective published standards. For PTO-powered equipment selection, the 30.3-hp PTO rating is the more directly relevant power value.

Kubota lists a rear PTO operating at 540 rpm at approximately 2,470 engine rpm for the HST version. PTO shaft speed, implement gearbox requirements, driveline overlap and shielding are critical. An implement that calls for more horsepower than the tractor can supply should not be considered compatible on horsepower assumptions alone.

Hitch lift capability

The official table gives a Category I three-point hitch with 1,985 lb lift capacity at the lift points and 1,433 lb at 24 inches behind the lift points. Those are two distinct manufacturer rating positions. A rear attachment can create different leverage and stability demands depending on its actual center of mass, not just its labeled shipping weight.

Hydraulics: distinguish main and steering pumps

The L3902's manufacturer specification reports 6.8 US gpm from the main hydraulic pump and 4.1 US gpm for power steering. The values describe separate pump outputs. Do not treat their sum as guaranteed flow from an implement coupler; verify actual auxiliary circuit performance, pressure and connection details for a loader, grapple or hydraulic implement.

Weight and dimensions

SpecificationL3902 HST 4WD
Published weight with ROPS2,921 lb
Wheelbase63.4 in
Approximate clearance in AG configuration13.4 in
Fuel tank capacity11.1 US gal
TransmissionHST, 3 speed ranges

The quoted weight is for the listed ROPS tractor configuration; a loader, filled tires, backhoe or rear counterweight will change actual mass and balance. For hauling, verify the complete loaded weight against trailer, hitch, vehicle and tie-down ratings.

Should you buy the L3902 HST or the L3302 HST?

Kubota gives the two HST variants the same published hitch rating, main pump capacity and ROPS weight, but the L3902 HST offers 4.2 additional published PTO horsepower (30.3 versus 26.1). That can matter to implement selection, but the correct choice also depends on the attachment's PTO requirement, ground speed, service access, dealer support and total price.

See the L3302 HST specifications and the comparison tool before deciding. Do not assume an increase in engine HP brings a proportional increase in loader lift or rear hitch rating.

Source and limits

The figures are reproduced as independently summarized, configuration-specific information from the Kubota USA L02 Series specification brochure, checked 2026-11-23. Manufacturer specifications can change; consult the exact operator manual before service or equipment use.

records.title: KIOTI CK2620 vs CK2620H: Gear vs Hydrostatic Tractor Specs
records.excerpt: Compare KIOTI CK2620 gear-drive and CK2620H hydrostatic models: identical 24.5 engine HP but different PTO power, weight and transmission controls.
records.content:
Choosing between the KIOTI CK2620 and CK2620H is not simply a decision between two tractors with the same engine horsepower. Both are listed at 24.5 engine HP, but the gear-drive CK2620 and hydrostatic CK2620H have different travel controls, published PTO power and machine weights. For the right buyer, those differences are more useful than the headline engine rating.

CK2620 versus CK2620H: manufacturer figures

SpecificationCK2620 (manual)CK2620H (HST)
Engine horsepower24.524.5
Engine modelKIOTI 3A165LWM-U4KIOTI 3A165LWM-U4
TransmissionManual, 12 forward / 12 reverseHydrostatic, 3 ranges
PTO horsepower19.518.7
Rear PTO speed540 rpm540 rpm
Three-point hitch categoryCategory 1Category 1
Hydraulic pump capacity11.7 US gpm11.7 US gpm
Fuel capacity9 US gal9 US gal
Published weight2,634 lb2,689 lb

All figures above are copied into an independent comparison from the exact US manufacturer model pages, checked November 23, 2026. PTO power is not gross engine power; pump capacity does not establish usable output through an auxiliary remote; weight changes with attachments and ballast.

What does 12F/12R manual transmission mean?

The CK2620 gear-drive tractor has a fixed set of transmission ratios listed as 12 forward and 12 reverse. Gear selection is a different operating experience from a hydrostatic pedal. Manual drive may suit operators comfortable choosing ratios for repetitive field or PTO tasks, but shifting and reversing frequency should be considered. Do not assume every gear can be changed without stopping or using the clutch; the correct operating manual defines the procedure.

What does 3-range HST mean?

The CK2620H combines a hydrostatic drive system with three operating ranges. Speed can be varied with the travel controls within a selected range, which is convenient for changing direction while handling materials, trimming near obstacles or doing close-quarters property work. Selecting the appropriate range is still important. Hydrostatic operation does not replace the need for brakes, safe slopes, traction or ballast.

Why is PTO horsepower different?

KIOTI reports 19.5 PTO hp for the manual CK2620 and 18.7 PTO hp for the CK2620H. Both list the same 24.5 engine hp. The 0.8-hp published difference is relevant if a rotary cutter or other implement has a minimum PTO requirement close to the tractor's available power. It is not a promise that one version will always complete a job faster in every field condition.

For PTO equipment, verify the attachment maker's minimum PTO power, required PTO shaft speed, hitch mounting, power take-off guarding and any ballast or hydraulic requirements. Our guide to engine vs PTO horsepower explains those ratings.

Which model can lift more?

Here it is especially important not to invent a matched comparison. KIOTI's page for the manual CK2620 lists a hitch lift value of 1,631 lb. The CK2620H manufacturer page contains separate hydraulic and hitch entries with different reported values. Neither model page clearly establishes a rating taken 24 inches behind the hitch lift points, so it would be misleading to compare either number directly with a Kubota brochure that explicitly uses that measurement position.

If lifting a heavy rotary cutter, ballast box or other rear implement is your decisive requirement, request the same load-center measurement and exact attachment recommendations for each tractor from the dealer. Remember the tractor's stability with a raised load also depends on tire and ballast configuration.

Do both work with the same attachments?

Both list Category 1 three-point hitches and 540-rpm rear PTO. That is a useful starting point, not a guarantee of universal interchangeability. The exact hitch geometry, PTO driveline, power requirement, tire clearance, implement weight, and hydraulic connection can still prevent safe fitment. For loaders, confirm the model-specific mount and quick-coupler system, not merely the brand name.

How to decide before buying

  1. Make a task list: mowing, tilling, loader cycling, snow work, driveway grading or long-duration PTO use.
  2. Test both transmissions: use realistic speeds and direction changes. Ask for an in-person demonstration.
  3. Check the specific implement: match horsepower and PTO shaft speed using the actual manual.
  4. Compare complete configurations: tire choice, ballast, loader, bucket, remotes and options all affect cost and usable performance.
  5. Check local service support: warranty access, parts availability and proximity to a capable dealer are part of ownership cost.

For source-backed individual records see CK2620 gear-drive specifications and CK2620H hydrostatic specifications, then use the machine comparison tool to compare more models.

Original references

KIOTI CK2620 official product specifications and KIOTI CK2620H official product specifications. Manufacturer tables checked November 23, 2026; values may change with tire, axle and equipment options.

records.title: Kubota L3302 vs L3902 HST: PTO HP, Hitch, Weight & Hydraulics
records.excerpt: Compare Kubota L3302 HST and L3902 HST using the official US brochure: 33 vs 37.5 gross HP, 26.1 vs 30.3 PTO HP, and matched hitch and hydraulic figures.
records.content:
The Kubota L3302 HST and L3902 HST are two versions of the Standard L compact tractor platform. They share many published dimensions and hitch specifications, but the L3902 HST delivers more rated engine and PTO power. The extra horsepower may matter for an implement-heavy property; it should not be confused with a higher three-point hitch or loader capacity.

Side-by-side official US specifications

SpecificationL3302 HST 4WDL3902 HST 4WD
Gross engine HP (SAE J1995)33.037.5
Net engine HP (SAE J1349)31.836.3
PTO power26.1 HP30.3 HP
Rear PTO / corresponding engine rpm540 / 2,470540 / 2,470
Transmission3-range HST3-range HST
Three-point hitchSAE Category ISAE Category I
Hitch lift at lift points1,985 lb1,985 lb
Hitch lift 24 in behind points1,433 lb1,433 lb
Main hydraulic pump6.8 US gpm6.8 US gpm
Separate power steering pump4.1 US gpm4.1 US gpm
Published ROPS weight2,921 lb2,921 lb
Fuel tank11.1 US gal11.1 US gal

This table is based on the Kubota Tractor Corporation US L02 Series brochure, not a mixture of dealer advertisements. It covers HST 4WD only. Manual/gear-drive L3302 and L3902 models have different published PTO horsepower and ROPS weights and must be compared separately.

What do the 4.2 extra PTO horsepower mean?

Published PTO power increases from 26.1 hp on the L3302 HST to 30.3 hp on the L3902 HST, a difference of 4.2 hp. In practical buying decisions, this may expand which rotary cutters, tillers or other shaft-driven implements meet the minimum PTO rating. It does not change an implement's gear box rating, shaft speed, tractor stability or hitch compatibility. If a mower needs more PTO power than the L3302 offers, the L3902 may be worth considering — but only after checking all other manufacturer requirements.

Do the tractors lift different weights?

Not in the particular three-point hitch table used here: Kubota publishes 1,433 lb at 24 inches behind the hitch points for both HST variants. The 1,985-lb lift-point rating is also identical. An engine-power increase should never be treated as an increase in certified hydraulic lifting capacity. The physical center of mass and safe ballast of an attachment matter.

Likewise, the brochure's 6.8-US-gpm main hydraulic pump figure is the same for both configurations. The separate steering pump is listed at 4.1 gpm. Hydraulic flow at an implement coupler is not established merely by adding those two values together.

What about weight and towing?

The manufacturer lists 2,921 lb with ROPS for both HST models. This excludes the actual mass of the machine after optional tires, loader, liquid-filled rear tires, ballast and implements are added. When loading either tractor onto a trailer, use the real configuration's total weight and check vehicle, trailer, hitch, ramp, brake and tie-down ratings.

Which is better for loader jobs?

Because these two HST variants share published hitch and main hydraulic-pump figures, more engine horsepower is not proof of more loader lift. If front-end loader work is your main use case, request the specific loader model's ratings at the same lift height and distance forward of the pivot pins. Verify the actual tractor with loader, counterweight, tire pressure and ground conditions. These parameters can govern safe handling more directly than an engine HP difference.

Questions to answer before choosing

  • What is your heaviest regularly used PTO-powered implement, and what exact minimum PTO power does its maker require?
  • Will work involve slopes, soft soil, frequent front-loader cycles or maneuvering around structures?
  • Which tires, hydraulic remotes, quick hitches and ballast are part of the actual dealer quote?
  • Does the extra PTO power justify the total purchase and ownership cost for your acreage and task list?

For detailed configurations, review L3302 HST specifications and L3902 HST specifications. Our interactive model comparison provides source context for additional machines.

Source and verification

Kubota L02 Series USA technical brochure, specification tables, pages 14–15. Checked November 23, 2026. Use your actual machine's operator manual and serial-specific information for service and safe operation.

records.title: Tractor 3-Point Hitch Lift Capacity: At Lift Points vs 24 Inches
records.excerpt: Understand why a tractor may lift 1,985 lb at its hitch points but only 1,433 lb at 24 inches behind them, and how this affects rear implements and counterweights.
records.content:
A tractor brochure might advertise two very different numbers for the same rear three-point hitch: lift capacity at the lift points and lift capacity 24 inches behind the lift points. These figures are not interchangeable. Understanding the distinction helps avoid buying an implement that is technically within a headline rating but too heavy or too far behind the tractor for safe handling.

What is the lift-point rating?

The lift points are the places where the lower hitch arms connect to an attachment. A published lift-point rating describes capacity at that specified position under the manufacturer's test conditions. It is not a general promise that every attachment weighing less than that number can be operated or raised safely. Three-point geometry, implement shape, ballast, hydraulics and stability all play a role.

What does “24 inches behind the lift points” mean?

Some manufacturers also publish a rating measured at a position 24 inches behind the lower link lift points. That moves the load farther from the tractor and changes leverage on the rear linkage and the entire machine. It is a useful standardized comparison reference when deciding between tractors and evaluating rear-mounted equipment whose weight is distributed away from the hitch.

An official Kubota example

Kubota's US L02 brochure gives the following three-point hitch ratings for the L3302 and L3902 series:

Where the capacity is measuredPublished value
At the lift points1,985 lb
24 inches behind the lift points1,433 lb

These are both manufacturer-listed ratings for the same series. The second figure is 552 lb lower because the specified load position is farther behind the tractor. That difference illustrates why comparing only the largest number from separate brochures is not fair to equipment buyers.

Our Kubota L3302 HST and Kubota L3902 HST model pages show the 24-inch value in a dedicated field. A specification sheet that does not name its test position should not be forced into that field.

What does the center of gravity of a rear implement change?

A rotary cutter, tiller, grading box or ballast box does not necessarily place all of its weight at the hitch pins. Much of the load can be located farther rearward. That greater distance increases the moment (turning effect) about the tractor's rear hitch. Its influence depends on the geometry, which is why the manufacturer's rating at a matching location is more meaningful than total attachment weight by itself.

The dimensions of a long rotary cutter, for example, differ from a compact ballast box even if their scales show the same weight. An attachment resting on the ground also behaves differently from one being fully lifted during transport. Do not treat a 24-inch rating as a formula that automatically validates every attachment whose center of gravity seems close to that distance.

Category 1 does not specify lifting capacity

A Category 1 hitch primarily describes a system of hitch dimensions and connections. Two tractors using Category 1 can have substantially different hydraulic lifting and stability limits. Knowing the category is essential to determine the connection type, but it does not establish how much a tractor can raise or safely carry. Quick-hitch compatibility can also require checking the attachment's geometry and floating top-link arrangement.

Do front loaders have the same issue?

They have a related measurement challenge, but different test locations: a front loader may be rated at the pivot pins or at a specified horizontal distance forward, sometimes at a particular lift height. The farther-forward location often produces a lower rating. When comparing two loader brochures, make sure you are comparing the same geometry, not just the maximum advertised weight.

What should you check before buying a rear implement?

  1. Get the actual attachment's total weight, approximate load-center location and manufacturer tractor requirements.
  2. Check your tractor's three-point hitch lift rating at the stated measuring position, not just its maximum figure.
  3. Confirm the three-point hitch category and any quick-hitch dimensional requirements.
  4. Check tire capacity, recommended front ballast, stability, clearance and ground conditions.
  5. Read the tractor and implement manuals for safe lifting, transport position, speed and maintenance.
  6. Ask the manufacturer or a qualified dealer for a configuration-specific assessment if the load is close to any stated limit.

When should you stop and ask for help?

If an attachment makes the front wheels light, causes unusual steering response, contacts tires or driveline components, or exceeds a documented rating, do not keep experimenting with higher throttle or more hydraulic pressure. Lower the implement safely, secure the machine as directed by the operator manual, and obtain an appropriate fitment or stability assessment.

Manufacturer reference

Kubota US L02 Series brochure, hydraulic and hitch specification table, checked November 23, 2026. This article explains published ratings; it is not an engineering certification of any specific implement or load combination.

records.title: Diesel Tractor Cranks but Won't Start: Safe First Checks
records.excerpt: A compact diesel tractor cranks but will not fire? Separate battery, fuel, cold-start and control issues before guessing at parts. Includes a safe diagnostic checklist and manufacturer references.
records.content:
A tractor that cranks normally but will not start presents a different problem from a tractor that does not crank at all. Hearing the starter turn the engine means the starting circuit is doing something; it does not establish that the battery, fuel supply, electronic controls or engine are working correctly. The right first step is to describe the symptom precisely, not to start replacing expensive injection components.

First: are you diagnosing a no-crank or a crank/no-start condition?

Observed behaviorFirst checks to discuss with the manual or technician
No sound or a single click when startingStarting authorization, PTO and transmission positions, battery terminals, charge state and manufacturer-specified interlocks
Engine turns over slowlyBattery condition, cable connections, temperature, oil viscosity specified by the manual and starter circuit condition
Engine cranks at normal speed but does not fireCorrect diesel fuel, fuel level, cold-start procedure, fuel filtration, contamination warnings and applicable engine indicators
Engine fires briefly, then stopsFuel restrictions, water in fuel, shutdown controls and model-specific codes or alarms

The table organizes questions; it is not a diagnosis. The exact interlocks and cold-start systems differ among sub-compact, compact and utility tractors. Some machines also have electronic shutoff or security features.

1. Make the machine safe before checking anything

Park on stable level ground when possible, lower the loader and other raised implements as instructed by the machine manual, select the proper transmission/parking position and disengage PTO drives. Keep people away from tires, attachments and the engine compartment. Never start a diesel tractor in a closed garage or shed: exhaust can contain deadly carbon monoxide, even when an engine only runs briefly.

Do not bypass seat, neutral, PTO or parking interlocks to force the starter to engage. Kubota's safety guidance emphasizes understanding the operator manual and maintaining safety systems; other manufacturers impose similar model-specific requirements.

2. Check what the dashboard and starter tell you

When the engine does not crank, note whether the dash lights come on, a relay clicks, the starter turns slowly or there is no response. If it cranks, listen for a consistent cranking speed rather than repeatedly holding the key for long periods. Cranking limits and cooling times are specified by the engine or tractor manufacturer and should not be exceeded.

Look for a low-voltage warning, a controller or immobilizer message, a glow-plug or cold-start indicator, or other fault code. Record the exact message and the machine's model and serial number. If a code appears, use the official troubleshooting information for that code rather than a generic list from another tractor.

3. Start with diesel fuel level and condition

Verify the fuel gauge against actual available fuel where the manual provides a safe check. Confirm that the machine is filled with the correct diesel fuel specified for its engine and climate. Do not add gasoline or kerosene in an attempt to thin winter diesel; Kubota Engine America explicitly advises against these mixtures because they can damage fuel-system components.

If the machine was stored, ask whether condensation, contaminated fuel, algae or seasonal fuel gelling could be involved. Follow the manual's approved water-separator and filter checks. Never loosen high-pressure common-rail fuel lines to look for injection pressure: escaping fuel can penetrate skin and require immediate medical care.

4. Consider the temperature and the correct starting procedure

A diesel engine may need a specified preheat cycle or manufacturer-directed cold-start routine. Consult the exact operator manual for glow-plug indicator timing, throttle settings and any block-heater equipment. Do not spray ether or starting fluid into a Kubota diesel: Kubota's official engine FAQ warns that ether and other gaseous starting enhancers can damage the engine. Do not assume another diesel engine supports such products without explicit manufacturer instructions.

If temperatures are very low, the correct diesel grade, battery performance and approved heating method can matter. Do not improvise with open flame or household heaters around fuel, wiring or hydraulic hoses.

5. Inspect only safe, accessible components

With the engine off and secured as instructed, visually inspect battery terminals and obvious loose or corroded connections. Check the water separator and service indicators as the manual permits. If an air filter warning is shown, inspect it according to the service instructions. Never run an engine with parts removed that are required for filtration or guarding.

If the tractor has recently had a fuel-filter change, fuel-system service or a completely empty tank, the manufacturer may specify a particular priming procedure. Do not assume the bleeding procedure of an older mechanical-injection tractor applies to a modern common-rail system.

6. What information helps a mechanic solve the problem faster?

  • Exact manufacturer, model, model year where known, serial number and displayed fault codes
  • Whether the starter is silent, clicking, slow or cranking at a normal speed
  • Recent fuel deliveries, filter replacements or the machine running completely out of fuel
  • Outside temperature, recent storage duration and whether the problem began suddenly or gradually
  • Recent maintenance, electrical work, aftermarket attachments or a discharged battery

Stop cranking and request professional service if you notice fuel leaks, unusual engine noises, damaged wiring, overheating signs, a runaway engine concern, or suspected high-pressure fuel-system damage. A diesel no-start condition can involve electrical, fuel-delivery, security or mechanical faults that cannot be isolated safely without proper diagnostic equipment.

Manufacturer sources and limits

This is a general symptom-based checklist, not a model-specific service instruction. The safety and fuel guidance comes from Kubota Engine America's official engine FAQ, Kubota USA maintenance check points, and Kubota USA tractor safety information, checked November 23, 2026. For John Deere machines, use the John Deere manuals portal. Your exact tractor manual takes precedence over generalized checks.

records.title: Compact Tractor Pre-Season Maintenance Checklist for Small Farms
records.excerpt: A practical pre-season compact tractor inspection covering fluids, tires, fuel, coolant, safety interlocks, PTO guards, hitch, belts and hoses, with manufacturer safety notes.
records.content:
Before a compact tractor goes back to mowing, tilling, loader work or seasonal field maintenance, spend time checking the systems that affect safe operation. A pre-season inspection will not replace the engine-hour-based service schedule, but it can reveal obvious problems before they interrupt work or damage attachments.

Use the checklist below as an inspection organizer. Do not treat it as a prescribed maintenance interval or a substitute for the operator's manual for your exact tractor. An L2502, BX2380, CK2620 and 1025R can have different lubrication points, filter numbers, fluid specifications and service-hour schedules.

Compact tractor walk-around checklist

AreaWhat to inspect before useWhy it matters
Parking area and groundVisible fluid leaks and obstacles beneath or near the tractorLeaks or hidden debris may indicate a problem before starting
TiresPressure, sidewall damage, tread condition and visible rim problemsStability, traction and load capacity change with tires and pressure
Engine and coolingOil level, coolant reservoir, radiator screen and debris buildupIncorrect levels and blocked cooling airflow can damage the engine
Fuel systemCorrect fuel, visible leakage, fuel filter and water separator indicationsContamination and air/fuel restrictions can contribute to no-start and poor running
Battery and electricalTerminal condition, cable damage, lights, warning indicatorsElectrical defects affect starting and safe operation
Controls and interlocksParking brake, PTO controls, safety switches and warning lampsProtective controls must work as described in the manual
PTO and implementsGuards, couplings, hitch pins, wear and any missing hardwareMoving driveline components present severe entanglement risks
Hydraulic attachmentsObvious hose damage, fittings, cylinder leakage, secure attachmentHigh-pressure hydraulic leaks and unsupported loads can be dangerous

These categories reflect the inspection priorities in Kubota's published daily maintenance points and the manufacturer's hay-season preparation checklist. They are useful for organizing pre-use checks even if your own tractor is another brand; the details of how to test or service each item must come from that manufacturer's manual.

Before starting: make the work area safe

Check that the tractor is secured, the parking brake is set, PTO is disengaged, and implements are supported or lowered as prescribed. Remove bystanders from the machine and the intended work area. If you must inspect underneath, do not rely on a hydraulic loader or hitch to support equipment. Use the manufacturer's safe support procedures and appropriate equipment.

Never run the engine in an enclosed garage or shed. Do not disconnect or defeat an operator-presence or neutral-start interlock simply because the machine has not been used for months. Kubota's official tractor safety guide emphasizes both points.

Inspect fluids without guessing the specifications

Engine oil, transmission/hydraulic fluid and engine coolant are separate systems on many compact tractors. Consult the correct model documentation for the viscosity, classification, fill level, inspection method and any specific service interval. A fuel tank or transmission listed as having a certain total capacity is not a license to pour that amount into a system that has not been fully drained.

If the engine is hot, do not open a pressurized cooling system. Allow the machine to cool and follow the manual's required steps. For a model-specific example, see Kubota BX2380 fluid capacities.

Tire inflation and ballast

Check the tires while the tractor is safely parked. The appropriate inflation pressure may depend on tire model, loader use, ballast and equipment weight. Turf, agricultural, industrial and hybrid tires can have different specifications. Use tire and tractor manufacturer instructions rather than copying the pressure from a neighbor's machine.

Inspect the actual ballast situation before loader tasks. A tractor is not automatically safe with heavy forks or a loaded bucket just because the engine has sufficient power. Front and rear axle loading, slope, tire grip and operating height all matter.

PTO, three-point hitch and attachments

Inspect PTO shields, guards, three-point hitch pins, locking devices and hydraulic hose routing with the equipment stopped. Any damaged or missing guard should be corrected before use. Confirm that the implement's shaft speed, horsepower needs and mounting geometry match your tractor. The hitch lift capacity guide explains why a lift-point rating and a 24-inch-back rating differ.

After long winter storage

Inspect the battery and connections, check for signs of rodents in wiring and air intake areas, and assess whether the stored diesel fuel is suitable for the current climate. If starting is difficult, use the proper engine manual's cold-start procedure; never improvise with ignition enhancers or open flames.

Once the manufacturer-prescribed pre-start inspection is complete and it is safe to operate, watch the dashboard for warnings and check for new leaks or unusual sounds. Keep a simple log of engine hours, inspection date and what was corrected. Those notes help with scheduled service and later resale.

When to stop and request service

Do not operate a tractor with compromised safety switches, damaged PTO guarding, a suspected high-pressure hydraulic leak, unstable steering, unexplained overheating, missing hitch hardware or significant fuel leaks. Repair or obtain professional service according to the relevant manufacturer's instructions before returning the machine to work.

Original manufacturer references

Kubota Maintenance Check Points; Kubota Hay Season Equipment Prep Checklist; Kubota Tractor Safety. Sources checked November 23, 2026. The checklist is general; for model-specific intervals, always consult the official operator manual.
